# Best open-ear earbuds for running

| Pick | Why | Price in the sources |
|---|---|---|
| **Bose Ultra Open Earbuds** (best overall clip-on) | Excellent sound, comfortable, stays put, and aims audio at the ear canal to limit leakage. Physical buttons are easy to use mid-run. Battery is about 7 hours (19.5 with the case) and it's only IPX4. | $199 on sale, $299 list |
| **Shokz OpenRun Pro 2** (best bone conduction) | Leaves your ears the most open, with fuller bass than older bone-conduction models. 12-hour battery, IP55, physical buttons. The neckband can interfere with long hair and winter hats. | $125 to $180 depending on retailer |
| **Shokz OpenDots 2** (best for long runs and wet weather) | 10 hours per charge (40 with the case) and an IP57 rating. Wired's top overall pick. | $200 |
| **Nothing Ear (Open)** (good value) | SoundGuys' top open-ear pick, with strong bass for the category, IP54, and a good app EQ. | $99 on sale, $149 list |
| **Soundcore AeroFit 2** (mid-budget ear hook) | Secure hook design, IP55, 10 hours per charge. | $79.99 at Amazon per SoundGuys |
| **JLab Flex Open** or **Soundpeats PearlClip Pro** (cheapest way to try the style) | Less bass and detail, but a low-risk test of clip-ons. | About $40 to $50 |

## How to choose
- **Best sound while running:** Bose Ultra Open. Wired notes Bose has a new pair coming soon, and Runner's World says the same, so you may want to wait or watch for discounts.
- **Maximum awareness of traffic:** Shokz OpenRun Pro 2. Runner's World calls it the best bone-conduction pick.
- **Rain, sweat, or marathon-length runs:** Shokz OpenDots 2.
- **Tight budget:** Nothing Ear (Open), AeroFit 2, or the $40 to $50 clip-ons.

Whichever you pick, keep the volume low enough to hear your surroundings. Open-ear designs don't guarantee safety, and they leak some sound.

## Where to buy
- **Soundcore AeroFit 2:** [Buy at Soundcore's US store via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-aerofit-2). This is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission at no cost to you. Dealectric lists a $129.99 store price and a code, AFSC20, that it says takes $25.99 off. That conflicts with SoundGuys' $99.99 MSRP and $79.99 Amazon price, so compare before buying, and note that the store's checkout has the final say on the code.
- **Bose, Shokz, and the other models:** The sources list current retailer prices, but I don't have direct product links for them. You can find them here:
  - [Runner's World roundup](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/): Bose, Shokz OpenRun Pro 2, OpenDots 2, JLab.
  - [WIRED roundup](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/): OpenDots 2, Bose, Soundpeats.
  - [SoundGuys open-ear roundup](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/): Nothing Ear (Open), AeroFit 2.
  - [WIRED OpenRun Pro 2 review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/)
  - [RTINGS Bose vs. OpenRun Pro 2 comparison](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946): RTINGS slightly favors the Bose for most people.

If you tell me your budget, whether you wear hats or glasses, and whether you use an iPhone or Android, I can narrow this to one pick.
